reason: Listing the contexts a browser has made, and reading a context's browser, which Strider has no collection for: Browser has pages and defaultContext, but no list of the contexts made through it, so the original's browser.contexts() can't be read. The whole test is those assertions

Creating a context with a null viewport, which Playwright uses to size pages to the window, and the validation errors for a device scale factor or a mobile flag given without one. Strider has no null: a context with no viewport option has no viewport declaration (its viewportSize is None), and a Viewport always holds a width and height, so those two settings can't be given without a size and the type refuses the combination before anything runs
Calling close() a second time. Strider has no close method: a context ends when its scope closes, and closing a scope again is Effect's behavior, not Strider's
Playwright's default user agent, read through its persistent-context `mode` fixture and its internal `_channel.defaultUserAgentForTest` hook
A device scale factor other than 1 for a context's viewport, which stock WebKit refuses with Unsupported (emulation.viewport.mobile and its scale), so the context can't be made there
Disabling JavaScript in a context, which Firefox can't emulate (emulation.javaScript), so the context can't be made with JavaScript off there
Taking a context offline, which stock WebKit can't emulate (emulation.network.offline), so the context can't be taken offline there
Emulating a color scheme in a context, which Firefox can't emulate (emulation.media), so the context's media can't be set there
Reading the popup a page opens, which stock WebKit can't report (popups.opener): Popup.next fails there, as WebKit can't say which page opened another
Emulating a color scheme in a context, which Firefox can't emulate (emulation.media), so the context's media can't be set there
